name: Aethoria
summary: A realm divided into seven provinces after a celestial impact fractured its moon.
description: Aethoria is a maritime fantasy realm whose broken moon drives magical tides. The Starfall created emberglass in the mountains, awakened drowned archives beneath the western sea, and destabilized the old royal roads.
facts: Magic intensifies during the silver tide every ninth night.
No monarch has ruled all seven provinces since the Salt Rebellion.
Fragments of the moon are called moonshards.

name: Lumenport
summary: A free harbor city built around nine ancient lighthouse towers.
description: Lumenport is the commercial heart of Aethoria. Its nine towers stabilize the magical tide around the bay, while tunnels beneath the oldest tower descend toward the Sunken Gate.
facts: The Lantern Court governs the harbor.
The ninth lighthouse has been silent for forty-two years.
Emberglass trade is legal only through the eastern quay.

name: The Ashwood
summary: A black-barked forest that remembers promises spoken beneath its canopy.
description: The Ashwood records sworn promises in the rings of its trees. Broken oaths manifest as pale hunting beasts, while honored agreements open safe paths through the forest.
facts: Open flame is forbidden by the Thorn Covenant.
Root paths move after every silver tide.
The Root Compass can reveal a path to the forest heart.

name: Glasspeak
summary: A volcanic mountain whose moonshard veins produce emberglass.
description: Glasspeak is mined through cooled lava tubes. Emberglass stores heat and memory, making it valuable for weapons, archives, and engines. The deepest mine is claimed by an ancient ember wyrm.
facts: The Ember Cartel controls most legal extraction.
Mining stops during the silver tide because the glass begins to sing.
The Emberglass Crown was forged in the first deep mine.

name: The Drowned Archive
summary: A submerged library accessible only when the western tide reverses.
description: The Drowned Archive contains records from before the Starfall. Air-filled reading chambers rotate through the structure as the tide changes, and tide wraiths guard books removed without permission.
facts: The archive opens for fifty-three minutes during a reverse tide.
Its catalog is encoded in the Bell of Nine Tides.
Kael Tidemark knows the safe entry sequence.

name: Vale of Mirrors
summary: A crystal valley where reflections can reveal possible futures.
description: The Vale of Mirrors contains natural crystal sheets that show probable futures rather than literal reflections. Predictions become less reliable when spoken aloud.
facts: Mirror moths feed on abandoned predictions.
Oria Vayne lost her shadow in the central mirror.
Metal weapons fracture the prophetic surfaces.

name: Obsidian Pass
summary: The only stable road between Glasspeak and the Free Coast.
description: Obsidian Pass is a narrow caravan route lined with black glass cliffs. Brann Ashward maintains its watchtowers while the Ember Cartel taxes every emberglass shipment.
facts: The northern bridge can carry only one loaded wagon at a time.
Hollow stags sometimes cross the pass before a broken oath is exposed.
A smuggler tunnel exits beneath watchtower three.

name: The Sunken Gate
summary: A sealed pre-Starfall transit gate hidden below Lumenport.
description: The Sunken Gate once connected the seven provincial capitals. It requires the Moon Key, the ninth lighthouse beam, and a living Tidebound navigator to open safely.
facts: Opening it without the ninth beam floods the lower city.
The Moon Key supplies the gate's missing lunar signature.
The Tidebound preserve the route sequence.

name: The Lantern Court
summary: Nine elected keepers who govern Lumenport and its lighthouse network.
description: The Lantern Court balances merchant interests against public safety. Each keeper controls one lighthouse, but the ninth seat has remained vacant since its tower went dark.
facts: Major decisions require six lantern votes.
Nera Quill serves as the court's archivist but has no vote.
The court secretly funds restoration of the ninth lighthouse.

name: The Ember Cartel
summary: A mining consortium controlling emberglass extraction and coastal distribution.
description: The Ember Cartel owns the largest Glasspeak mines and maintains private guards along Obsidian Pass. It seeks the Emberglass Crown to legitimize a permanent monopoly.
facts: The cartel controls roughly seventy percent of legal emberglass.
Its ledgers use heat-reactive ink.
It has placed a bounty on Sylva Morn.

name: The Tidebound
summary: Navigators trained to sense lunar tides and traverse drowned roads.
description: Tidebound navigators tattoo route songs onto their arms. Their order was outlawed after the Salt Rebellion, but small crews still guide ships and protect the Drowned Archive.
facts: Only living Tidebound navigators can stabilize the Sunken Gate.
Their route songs change after each Starfall anniversary.
Kael Tidemark leads the remaining western crew.

name: The Thorn Covenant
summary: Wardens who enforce oath law and protect the Ashwood.
description: The Thorn Covenant mediates promises made within the Ashwood and hunts oathbreakers before the forest creates hollow stags to do so.
facts: Its wardens carry no metal inside the forest.
Sylva Morn is the youngest covenant speaker.
The covenant signed the Ashwood Pact with Lumenport.

name: Elian Voss
summary: A disgraced lighthouse engineer attempting to relight Lumenport's ninth tower.
description: Elian designed a moonshard lens for the ninth lighthouse but was blamed when its first test failed. He now works beneath the tower and believes the failure was sabotage.
facts: He needs the Moon Key to calibrate the replacement lens.
He distrusts the Ember Cartel.
He knows how to prevent the Sunken Gate from flooding Lumenport.

name: Nera Quill
summary: The Lantern Court archivist who discovered the Sunken Gate restoration records.
description: Nera is a meticulous historian who compares heat-ink ledgers with pre-Starfall maps. She suspects the Ember Cartel sabotaged the ninth lighthouse.
facts: She can read heat-reactive cartel ink.
She keeps a hidden copy of the gate sequence.
She is Elian Voss's closest ally.

name: Brann Ashward
summary: A veteran road warden responsible for keeping Obsidian Pass open.
description: Brann commands three watchtowers and knows the cartel's smuggling routes. He carries an unpaid oath to protect Sylva Morn, which draws hollow stags toward him.
facts: He knows the location of the smuggler tunnel.
His oath to protect Sylva remains unfulfilled.
He refuses cartel payment.

name: Sylva Morn
summary: A Thorn Covenant speaker trying to renew the failing Ashwood Pact.
description: Sylva can hear promises stored in tree rings. She stole evidence that the Ember Cartel burned an oath-tree while expanding a secret mine.
facts: The cartel has placed a bounty on her.
She can safely command the Root Compass.
She needs Brann to publicly fulfill his protection oath.

name: Kael Tidemark
summary: Leader of the remaining Tidebound crew and keeper of drowned routes.
description: Kael memorized the route songs needed for the Drowned Archive and Sunken Gate. He will help Lumenport only if the Lantern Court clears the Tidebound of treason.
facts: He knows the safe entry sequence to the Drowned Archive.
His living tide mark can stabilize the Sunken Gate.
He survived the Salt Rebellion as a child.

name: Oria Vayne
summary: A prophet whose shadow remains trapped in the Vale of Mirrors.
description: Oria interprets future reflections but refuses to state predictions directly. Her missing shadow acts independently during the silver tide.
facts: She predicted that the Emberglass Crown must remain unclaimed.
Mirror moths gather around her written prophecies.
Her shadow knows where the Crown was hidden.

name: Hollow Stag
summary: A pale forest predator formed when an important oath is broken.
description: A hollow stag tracks the person responsible for a broken promise. It ignores anyone who truthfully acknowledges the oath and can be dismissed when restitution begins.
facts: It cannot cross a circle of living thorn.
It follows unresolved oaths rather than scent.
Killing one causes another to emerge the next night.

name: Sarthuun the Ember Wyrm
summary: An ancient wyrm sleeping around the richest emberglass vein in Glasspeak.
description: Sarthuun absorbs stored memories from emberglass. The wyrm attacks miners who carry forged memories but bargains for authentic stories.
facts: Cold seawater hardens its scales temporarily.
It remembers the original owner of the Emberglass Crown.
It has not left the deep mine for ninety years.

name: Tide Wraith
summary: A drowned guardian that retrieves knowledge stolen from the Drowned Archive.
description: Tide wraiths pass through water and written ink. They ignore visitors who return copied knowledge before the reverse tide ends.
facts: They cannot read text written in salt.
The Bell of Nine Tides can delay them for nine breaths.
They pursue stolen books across any body of seawater.

name: Mirror Moth
summary: A crystal-winged insect that consumes discarded possible futures.
description: Mirror moths erase futures that observers reject. A swarm can make one improbable outcome temporarily more likely by consuming its alternatives.
facts: Their wings become dark after feeding on a violent future.
They follow Oria Vayne during the silver tide.
They are harmless unless trapped near an active prophecy.

name: The Moon Key
summary: A moonshard instrument required to reactivate pre-Starfall gates.
description: The Moon Key stores a stable copy of the old moon's magical signature. It can calibrate the ninth lighthouse and unlock the Sunken Gate when used by a Tidebound navigator.
facts: It is currently hidden inside the Root Compass.
It becomes visible only under ninth-night moonlight.
Elian Voss needs it to repair the lighthouse lens.

name: The Emberglass Crown
summary: A crown that transfers stored memories from a ruler to a chosen successor.
description: The Crown was forged before the Salt Rebellion. It grants no legal authority by itself, but the Ember Cartel claims possession would prove a right to govern Cinder Reach.
facts: Oria Vayne predicted disaster if anyone claims it.
Sarthuun remembers its original owner.
It is hidden in a future reflection rather than a physical vault.

name: The Root Compass
summary: A living wooden compass that maps the moving paths of the Ashwood.
description: The Root Compass points toward fulfilled promises. Sylva Morn can command it safely, and its hollow center secretly contains the Moon Key.
facts: It refuses to guide anyone currently breaking an oath.
Its needle is a living thorn.
The Moon Key is concealed in its central seed chamber.

name: The Bell of Nine Tides
summary: A bronze handbell encoding the catalog and opening rhythm of the Drowned Archive.
description: Each ring corresponds to a moving archive chamber. The correct nine-note sequence reveals a requested subject and delays tide wraiths for nine breaths.
facts: Kael Tidemark knows seven of the nine tones.
The eighth tone is recorded in Nera Quill's hidden map.
The ninth tone can only be heard during a reverse tide.

name: The Gates Below
summary: Restore the ninth lighthouse and open the Sunken Gate without flooding Lumenport.
description: The mission requires recovering the Moon Key from the Root Compass, clearing the Tidebound of treason, recruiting Kael Tidemark, and calibrating Elian Voss's moonshard lens.
facts: The gate must be opened during the silver tide.
Skipping the lighthouse repair floods the lower city.
Kael and Elian must operate their components simultaneously.

name: The Crown Without Flame
summary: Prevent the Ember Cartel from retrieving the Emberglass Crown from a future reflection.
description: The party must question Sarthuun, interpret Oria Vayne's indirect prophecy, and use mirror moths to collapse the future in which the Cartel claims the Crown.
facts: Destroying the Crown releases every memory stored inside it.
The Cartel plans to enter the Vale during the next silver tide.
Sarthuun will trade information for a true royal memory.

name: The Forest Oath
summary: Renew the Ashwood Pact before hollow stags overwhelm Obsidian Pass.
description: Sylva must expose the Cartel's burned oath-tree while Brann publicly fulfills his promise to protect her. The Root Compass then reveals the forest heart where the pact can be renewed.
facts: Killing hollow stags cannot solve the underlying broken oaths.
Brann's public restitution opens the first safe path.
The Cartel evidence is hidden in watchtower three.

name: The Silent Bell
summary: Recover all nine tones of the Bell of Nine Tides and access a pre-Starfall record.
description: Kael knows seven tones, Nera's hidden map contains the eighth, and the ninth must be recorded inside the Drowned Archive during a reverse tide.
facts: The full sequence can locate any surviving archive chamber.
A wrong tone summons two tide wraiths.
Salt-written notes remain invisible to the guardians.

name: The Starfall
summary: The celestial impact that shattered Aethoria's moon 312 years ago.
description: Moon fragments struck Glasspeak and the western sea, creating emberglass and the reverse tides. The impact also disabled the provincial gate network.
facts: The current calendar counts years After Starfall.
Moonshards retain fragments of the old moon's magical signature.
The Sunken Gate failed on the same night.

name: The Salt Rebellion
summary: A coastal uprising that ended centralized rule eighty-seven years ago.
description: The provinces rejected the crown's control of navigation and salt routes. The Tidebound were falsely blamed for sinking the royal fleet and were outlawed after the rebellion.
facts: The last monarch disappeared during the final battle.
The Tidebound records contradict the official account.
Lumenport became a free city afterward.

name: The Ashwood Pact
aliases: Pacte de la Forêt de Cendre
summary: A living treaty between Lumenport and the Thorn Covenant.
description: The pact keeps the road through the Ashwood open in exchange for a ban on fire and mining. The Ember Cartel's secret burned oath-tree is causing the treaty to fail.
facts: The pact must be renewed every twenty-seven years.
Its current renewal is eleven days overdue.
Only a Thorn speaker and a Lumenport keeper can renew it.
